components.css: .ds-label { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; margin: 6px 0 3px; font: 600 13px system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; color: #0f172a; } .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 18px; height: 18px; border-radius: 50%; background: #0f172a; color: #fff; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 700; } .ds-input { width: 100%; box-sizing: border-box; padding: 7px 8px; border: 1px solid #cbd5e1; border-radius: 5px; background: #fff; color: #0f172a; font: 15px system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; caret-color: #c026d3; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #64748b; } .ds-input:focus-visible { border-color: #c026d3; outline: 1px solid #c026d3; } @media (pointer: coarse) { .ds-input { min-height: 44px; font-size: 16px; } }

narrative.overview:
vlcbici is a calm guide in a stranger's pocket. The map leads; the panel quietly says what to do next. A visitor who does not know Valencia stands on a street with a phone in one hand and needs three answers fast: where to get a bike, where to ride, where to give it back. Every visual decision serves that glance.

The system is native map-app plain. It uses the platform's own font, flat white panels and controls that look like the ones people already know from map apps. The brand does not decorate; it lives in one place: the magenta course of the bike ride and the stations that start and end it. Slate carries the text and the main action. Status colours appear only where they report real station data.

Density is moderate and compact: a 360px floating panel on desktop, a bottom sheet on phones, small type steps, short gaps. Nothing in the panel competes with the map for attention.
keyCharacteristics: Map first; the panel is a quiet tool on top of it.
One brand colour, Route Magenta, reserved for the planned bike course and its stations.
Slate ink for text and the primary action, never the brand colour.
Colour always has a job: wayfinding (A/B), course, or station status.
System font, flat surfaces, one soft shadow for the floating panel.

rules.name: The One Course Rule
rules.body: Route Magenta marks the planned bike course and the stations that bound it. It is not a button colour, a heading colour or a decoration. If something magenta is not part of the trip or a focus/selection state, it is wrong.

rules.name: The Data Owns Its Colours Rule
rules.body: Green, orange, yellow, red and grey belong to station status, blue and cyan to bike lanes. New UI never reuses them for anything else.

rules.name: The Pin Equals Badge Rule
rules.body: The A/B badges in the panel and popups always use the same colours as the A/B pins on the map. Change one, change both (`style.css` tokens and `app.js` pin colours).

rules.name: The Small Steps Rule
rules.body: Sizes stay within 11–18px. Hierarchy comes from weight (400/600/700) and colour (ink vs. muted), not from big size jumps; the map is the only large element.

rules.name: The Float Only Rule
rules.body: A shadow means "this sits on the map". Nothing inside the panel gets one.

dos: Do keep Route Magenta (#c026d3) for the bike course, its stations, the "B" mark, the logo accent and focus.
Do use Slate Ink (#0f172a) for the primary action and body text.
Do keep A/B badges and A/B map pins in the same colours.
Do keep every status colour paired with text: the legend, popup labels or a message.
Do use the 5px radius for controls and cards, full circles for anything that marks a point.
Do use the existing neutral tokens (`--ink`, `--muted`) for new text. Some older rules still use plain greys (#555, #fafafa, #e5e5e5, #f3f4f6); move them to slate tokens when you touch them.
donts: Don't use blue or cyan for the route or the brand; the CyclOSM and city network layers already draw bike lanes in those colours.
Don't use green, orange, yellow, red or grey for anything except station status and errors.
Don't put shadows on elements inside the panel.
Don't use web fonts or large display type; the map is the hero.
Don't use Valenbisi, JCDecaux or City of Valencia logos or brand styling; the app is unofficial.
